scientific.integrity: The scalar equality \(Z(M_{2n})=4\) is explicitly credited as prior work. The retained contribution is a direct all-orders classification of minimum sets, a five-orbit decomposition for \(n\ge4\), and the exact leading coefficient \(13n\). The proof is independent of the finite verifier, which exhaustively stress-tests all four-subsets through order \(24\).
limitations: The five-orbit theorem is for \(n\ge4\); the boundary graph \(M_6\cong K_{3,3}\) is treated separately.
Only minimum zero forcing sets are classified; no formula is claimed for larger coefficients of the zero forcing polynomial.
Targeted literature and database searches reduce but do not eliminate the risk of an unindexed equivalent classification.

title: Minimum zero forcing sets of Möbius ladders
